name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
summary: EU, US and other passport holders all need a permit or citizenship to live here; there is no free movement. The cheapest way to a passport is the Sustainable Island State Contribution from USD 250,000 (or USD 250,000 to a public benefit project; real estate from USD 325,000). Ordinary residence routes (homeowner, self-sufficient temporary residence) exist but could only be sourced from secondary guides.
naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation under the Citizenship Act is reported at 14 years of residence immediately before the application (government service can shorten it); good character required. Not read in full from the statute.
dual_citizenship_note: The Citizenship Unit states that dual citizenship is allowed for CBI citizens.

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: Sustainable Island State Contribution (SISC)
routes.summary: A non-refundable contribution of USD 250,000 to the national fund gives citizenship with no residence requirement.
routes.requirements: Minimum USD 250,000 for the main applicant (earlier note: includes family of up to four, with USD 25,000 per extra dependant under 18 and USD 50,000 per extra dependant 18+; not re-verified this pass). Applicant must be 18+, pass due diligence and meet financial criteria. Disqualified if refused citizenship or a visa by any visa-free partner country (unless since obtained), criminal record or active investigation, or bankruptcy within 10 years. Applications from Afghanistan, Belarus, Iran, Iraq, North Korea and Russia are not accepted; nationality exclusions apply within the OTHER group. Applications go through an authorised agent.
routes.investment_options: SISC USD 250,000; Public Benefit Option USD 250,000 (approved projects); Developer real estate USD 325,000; private real estate USD 600,000.
routes.fees_note: Due diligence and processing fees not re-verified on the Citizenship Unit pages reached this pass (earlier note: USD 10,000 main applicant, USD 7,500 per dependant 16+). See open questions.
routes.physical_presence: None. The Citizenship Unit states there is no residency requirement.
routes.family: Spouse, children under 18 (to 30 if in full-time study and supported), disabled adult children, and parents 55+ supported by and living with the applicant.
routes.tax_note: No personal income tax in St Kitts and Nevis, but CBI citizens must file a final return and obtain a clearance certificate on emigrating (earlier Deloitte note). Citizenship alone does not end tax residence elsewhere.

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: Real estate
routes.summary: Buy into an approved development from USD 325,000, or an exclusive private property from USD 600,000.
routes.requirements: Developer real estate in an approved development: minimum USD 325,000. Private real estate sale: at least USD 600,000. Reported holding period 7 years (earlier note and secondary sources; not stated on the pages read). Applicant must be 18+, pass due diligence and meet financial criteria. Disqualified if refused citizenship or a visa by any visa-free partner country (unless since obtained), criminal record or active investigation, or bankruptcy within 10 years. Applications from Afghanistan, Belarus, Iran, Iraq, North Korea and Russia are not accepted; nationality exclusions apply within the OTHER group.
routes.investment_options: Developer real estate USD 325,000; private property USD 600,000.
routes.fees_note: Earlier note: post-approval fees USD 25,000 main applicant, USD 15,000 spouse, USD 10,000 per child under 18. Not re-verified.
routes.physical_presence: None stated by the Citizenship Unit (no residency requirement).
routes.tax_note: Citizenship alone does not make you tax resident anywhere.

Disqualified if refused citizenship or a visa by any visa-free partner country (unless since obtained), criminal record or active investigation, or bankruptcy within 10 years. Applications from Afghanistan, Belarus, Iran, Iraq, North Korea and Russia are not accepted; nationality exclusions apply within the OTHER group.

routes.name: Homeowner / self-sufficient residence
routes.summary: People who own property or can show they support themselves and have health insurance can get annual residence permits; a permanent route is reported but unsourced.
routes.requirements: Per one advisory guide only: proof of self-sufficiency and health insurance, renewed yearly; a permanent track reportedly linked to property of about USD 350,000 held for 7 years. No official source found for thresholds, fees or permit names.

sources.title: Residency in St Kitts and Nevis: routes and costs (2026)

open_questions: Government and due diligence fees for each CBI option were not on the pages reached; earlier note says due diligence USD 10,000 main / USD 7,500 per dependant 16+. Verify on the Citizenship Unit fee pages.
Holding period for CBI real estate (7 years reported) not confirmed this pass.
Official thresholds and permit names for ordinary residence (homeowner, self-sufficient, permanent) not found; the USD 350,000 / 7 year permanent figure is unsourced.
Whether St Kitts and Nevis has a digital nomad visa: sources conflict (one describes a 'Remote Work in Paradise' resident visa, others say none).
Earlier note: from 14 April 2026 CBI citizens must enrol in a biometric passport programme (deadline 31 July 2027); not re-verified.
Ordinary naturalisation: 14 years read from a statute excerpt and secondary summaries; conflicting 7+7 year account in one guide.
Chairman's Update December 2025 and Citizenship Unit Act 2024 referenced on the CIU page but not read.
ECCIRA start date: sources conflict (April 2026, Q2 2026, September 2026, 'late 2026', or not yet operational as of 8 August 2026). Check eccira.org.

Reported European Commission letter of 25 June 2026 asking the Eastern Caribbean states to end citizenship programmes by 1 June 2028 comes from one professional source (Passport Legacy); not checked against a Commission document.
